microtheory.name: proof_model_theory
microtheory.definition: Mathematical logic: proof theory + model theory. Cut elimination, ordinal analysis, compactness, Löwenheim-Skolem, ultraproducts, definability, categoricity. The formal foundations of mathematical reasoning. Substrate analogue: substrate's meta-level reasoning about its own inference.

concepts.name: proof_theory
concepts.definition: Gentzen, Hilbert. Mathematical study of proofs as formal objects. Substrate analogue: substrate's reasoning-about-derivation.

concepts.name: cut_rule
concepts.definition: Sequent calculus rule combining proofs. (Γ⊢A, A,Δ⊢B) → (Γ,Δ⊢B). Substrate analogue: substrate's proof composition.

concepts.name: cut_elimination_theorem
concepts.definition: Gentzen 1934. Every proof reducible to cut-free proof. Subformula property. Substrate analogue: substrate's proof-normalization.

concepts.name: normal_form_proof
concepts.definition: Cut-free proof. Subformula property holds. Substrate analogue: substrate's minimal-derivation form.

concepts.name: ordinal_analysis
concepts.definition: Measuring strength of formal theories by which ordinals they can prove well-founded. Substrate analogue: substrate's strength-of-theory measure.

concepts.name: model_theory
concepts.definition: Tarski. Study of mathematical structures as models of formal theories. Substrate analogue: substrate's structure-based semantics.

concepts.name: structure_first_order
concepts.definition: Set with named operations + relations. Models of FOL. Substrate analogue: substrate's typed-graph as structure.

concepts.name: elementary_equivalence
concepts.definition: Two structures satisfy same first-order sentences. Substrate analogue: substrate's behavior-equivalence.

concepts.name: isomorphism_structure
concepts.definition: Bijection preserving structure. Indistinguishable. Substrate analogue: substrate's structural-identity.

concepts.name: homomorphism_structure
concepts.definition: Map preserving structure. May not be bijective. Substrate analogue: substrate's structure-preserving transformation.

concepts.name: compactness_theorem
concepts.definition: FOL: set of sentences has model iff every finite subset has. Substrate analogue: substrate's local-global consistency.

concepts.name: lowenheim_skolem_theorem
concepts.definition: FOL theory with infinite model has models of every infinite cardinality. Substrate analogue: substrate's scale-flexibility.

concepts.name: skolem_paradox
concepts.definition: Set theory has countable models even though it proves uncountable sets exist. Substrate analogue: substrate's representational paradox.

concepts.name: categoricity
concepts.definition: Theory categorical iff all models isomorphic. FOL categorical only for finite structures. Substrate analogue: substrate's unique-realization theory.

concepts.name: definability
concepts.definition: Property/relation expressible in language. Substrate analogue: substrate's expressible-Concept set.

concepts.name: tarski_undefinability
concepts.definition: Truth predicate for arithmetic not definable IN arithmetic. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-reference limit.

concepts.name: beth_definability
concepts.definition: Implicit definability = explicit definability in FOL. Substrate analogue: substrate's definitional completeness.

concepts.name: type_theory_logic
concepts.definition: Russell + Whitehead, Church, Martin-Löf. Stratified hierarchy of types avoiding paradoxes. Foundation of proof assistants. Substrate analogue: substrate's typed-Concept hierarchy.

concepts.name: simple_type_theory
concepts.definition: Church 1940. Basic types + function types. Substrate analogue: substrate's primitive + function types.

concepts.name: dependent_type_theory
concepts.definition: Martin-Löf. Types depending on values. Foundation of Coq, Agda, Lean. Substrate analogue: substrate's value-dependent types.

concepts.name: homotopy_type_theory
concepts.definition: HoTT. Types as spaces, equality as paths. Univalent foundations. Substrate analogue: substrate's geometric type interpretation.

concepts.name: decidability
concepts.definition: Algorithm exists deciding every formula. Propositional decidable; FOL undecidable (Church + Turing). Substrate analogue: substrate's algorithmic-verification limit.

concepts.name: godel_completeness
concepts.definition: Gödel 1929. FOL: valid implies provable. Substrate analogue: substrate's complete provability for valid.

concepts.name: godel_first_incompleteness
concepts.definition: Gödel 1931. Consistent system strong enough for arithmetic contains true unprovable sentence G. Substrate analogue: substrate's truth-beyond-provability.

concepts.name: godel_second_incompleteness
concepts.definition: System can't prove its own consistency. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-consistency unprovability.

concepts.name: proof_assistant
concepts.definition: Software helping construct + verify proofs. Coq, Isabelle, Lean, Agda. Substrate analogue: substrate's verification tool.

concepts.name: automated_theorem_prover
concepts.definition: Software proving theorems automatically. Vampire, E, Prover9. Substrate analogue: substrate's autonomous derivation.

concepts.name: sat_solver
concepts.definition: Decides propositional satisfiability. Very efficient despite NP-completeness. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-finder.

concepts.name: smt_solver
concepts.definition: Satisfiability Modulo Theories. SAT + theory-specific reasoning. Substrate analogue: substrate's theory-augmented search.

concepts.name: reverse_mathematics
concepts.definition: Friedman 1975. Identifying minimum axioms needed to prove theorems. Substrate analogue: substrate's minimal-axiom analysis.

concepts.name: consistency_strength
concepts.definition: Comparing theories by which prove others' consistency. Substrate analogue: substrate's theory-strength ordering.

rules.name: cut_elimination_normalizes_proofs
rules.head: the substrate has a proof using cut rule
rules.body: the proof reduces to cut-free form with subformula property. Gentzen. Substrate's proof-normalization.

rules.name: compactness_links_local_global_consistency
rules.head: the substrate has an infinite set of sentences
rules.body: it has model iff every finite subset has model. Substrate's local-global consistency principle.

rules.name: lowenheim_skolem_relativizes_cardinality
rules.head: the substrate's first-order theory has infinite model
rules.body: it has models of every infinite cardinality. Substrate's scale-flexibility.

rules.name: tarski_undefinability_limits_self_reference
rules.head: the substrate represents truth within itself
rules.body: the truth predicate cannot be definable internally. Substrate's self-reference limit.

rules.name: godel_second_blocks_self_consistency_proof
rules.head: the substrate is consistent + strong enough for arithmetic
rules.body: it cannot prove its own consistency. Substrate's self-consistency limitation.
